Attorney General to take over as a special prosecutor overseeing the alleged rape case
at Cornell University. Hochul says she's lost confidence in the local prosecutor, NPR's
Brian Mann reports. Hochul said in a statement she no longer has confidence in Tompkins County

without seeing a full transcript of the woman's account of the alleged rape.
New information has raised serious questions about how this case was handled, Hochul wrote.
She added that the alleged victim deserves to know that every fact will be examined and

didn't respond to NPR's request for comment. In a civil lawsuit filed last month, the woman alleges

case was mishandled. Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York. Attorneys for Tennessee death row inmate
Krista Pike say Pike is still alive but in critical condition. They spoke to reporters
Thursday after the state's failed attempt to execute Pike by lethal injection for a 1995
murder when she was 18. Catherine Sweeney of member station WPLN was a media witness.
The warden came over the loudspeaker after, I mean, you know, two hours of trying. The warden
came over the loudspeaker and said you need to leave, so we did. We go outside to do the
press conference that's part of the witness process and ambulances come to pick her up.
There's this wave of emergency vehicles and they carted her away with sirens on. So we
guessed she was still alive. It remains uncertain what went wrong. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee
called the failed execution a tragedy. He has ordered a third-party review. Protests by French
high school students demanding better learning conditions have turned violent with nearly 2000
arrest schools and vehicles set on fire and at least 300 police and firefighters injured.
And Paris Eleanor Beardsley reports 400 schools across the country will be closed Friday.
A protest against rundown buildings and overcrowded classrooms started last week
in one high school in the Paris suburbs before spreading to more than a thousand schools across
the country. The students' demands were seen as legitimate but scenes of chaos and confrontations
between police and massed bands of young people shown on the TV news are shocking the French.
The prime minister who organized a crisis cell Thursday has accused the far left of
encouraging the protesters for political reasons. But even far left leader Jean-Luc
Médecins who has supported the protesters seemed overtaken by the violent turn of events.
He called on the young people to stop the destruction saying it serves no purpose.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris. This is NPR News.
The U.S. Supreme Court has agreed to review a Trump administration policy
that denies bond hearings for detained immigrants. The justices will consider whether immigrants
have a right to a hearing to determine if they should remain detained while challenging their
possible deportation. The Trump administration has restored specialized suicide prevention service
for LGBTQ+ youth through the 988 suicide and crisis lifeline. The service returned on September
30th, more than 14 months after it was abruptly shut down, NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports.
The 988 helpline had received nearly 1.3 million contacts from LGBTQ+ youth over three years before
it was shut down. Those contacts included calls, texts and online chats. In January of this year,
the U.S. Senate passed a bipartisan bill to fund the federal health department
that also mandated the restoration of the specialized service on 988. Democratic
Senator Tammy Baldwin of Wisconsin is a lead sponsor of that legislation.
I hope the restoration will restore trust and faith that people should indeed reach out to 988.
LGBTQ+ youth can once again access specialized crisis support tailored for them by dialing 988
and then pressing option 3. Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
